title: Culture and establishment of self-renewing human and mouse adult liver and pancreas 3D organoids and their genetic manipulation.
markdown:
## Protocol: Protocol for culture and establishment of self-renewing human adult liver organoids from liver tissue and their genetic manipulation

### Overview

This protocol outlines the procedures for establishing, maintaining, and genetically manipulating self-renewing human adult liver organoids derived from liver tissue. The workflow includes initial tissue dissociation, optional FACS sorting of ductal stem cells, seeding in basement matrix, expansion culture, passaging, cryopreservation/thawing, and viral transduction with subsequent selection.

### Materials/Reagents

Basal medium, wash medium, human liver digestion solution, TrypLE solution, DNaseI (10 mg/ml), blocking solution (DMEM/GlutaMAX with 2% FBS), antibody staining reagents, FACS sorting medium, expansion medium, isolation medium, ROCK inhibitor (Y-27632, 10 µM), basement matrix (BME2 for human material), freezing medium (containing DMSO), puromycin (1 µg/ml), Plat-E cells, DMEM + 10% FBS, blasticidin (10 µg/ml), retroviral DNA construct, Opti-MEM, Lipofectamine 2000, polybrene, transduction medium, Matrigel (for mouse material, if applicable).

### Equipment

Fine scissors, 100-mm Petri dish, 15-ml centrifuge tubes, 10-ml pipette, 70-µm filter, 40-µm filter, standard hemocytometer, FACS sorter, glass Pasteur pipettes, flame source, table-top microcentrifuge, 24-well and 48-well plates (suspension plates required for human cells), water bath (37 °C), −80 °C freezer, liquid nitrogen storage, ultracentrifuge, 0.45-µm filters, 25-ml syringe, 50-ml ultracentrifuge tubes, retort stand, Parafilm, 1.5-ml microcentrifuge tubes.

### Safety & Sterility

Maintain aseptic conditions throughout tissue processing and cell culture. Handle DMSO in freezing medium with care as it is toxic to cells at room temperature; minimize exposure time. Use caution when handling liquid nitrogen and ultracentrifuge tubes. Ensure proper disposal of biological waste.

## Reagent Preparation

### 2-3 weeks before use

1. Prepare Rspo1-conditioned growth medium by supplementing DMEM with 10% FBS and 150 µg/ml Zeocin, then store at 4 °C for up to 1 week. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->

## Cryopreservation and Thawing

### Cryopreservation

1. Precool a freezing container at 4 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S01 -->
2. Proceed as described in Steps 8-12 of the main PROCEDURE, then gently resuspend the cell aggregates in 500 µl of cold freezing medium per one well (24-well plates) or two wells (48-well plates). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S02 -->
3. Transfer the suspension to cryovials (500 µl each) and place them in the precooled cell freezing container, then transfer to −80 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S03 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: The freezing medium contains DMSO, which is toxic to the cells at room temperature; therefore, use cold freezing medium and do not exceed a total of 5 min between adding the freezing medium to the cells and transferring them to −80 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S04 -->
4. After a minimum of 24 h at −80 °C, transfer cryovials to liquid nitrogen for long-term storage. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S05 -->
> **Operational constraint:** PAUSE POINT: Cells can be stored in liquid nitrogen for long-term storage (1-2 years). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S06 -->
5. Precool a freezing container at 4 °C. For each cryovial tube, ensure that at least one confluent well (24-well plates) or two confluent wells (48-well plates) has been grown before freezing. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S130 -->
6. Proceed as described in Steps 8-12 of the main PROCEDURE, then gently resuspend the cell aggregates in 500 µl of cold freezing medium per one well (24-well plates) or two wells (48-well plates). Transfer the suspension to cryovials (500 µl each) and place them in the precooled cell freezing container. Transfer to −80 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S131 -->
7. After a minimum of 24 h at −80 °C, transfer cryovials to liquid nitrogen for long-term storage. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S132 -->

### Thawing

1. Warm a water bath to 37 °C, prepare a 15-ml tube with 10 ml of basal medium prewarmed to 37 °C, and prewarm an appropriate 24-well plate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S01 -->
2. Incubate the cryovial in the 37 °C water bath, stopping when the ice is almost completely thawed, then transfer the thawed cell aggregates to the prewarmed 15-ml centrifuge tube containing basal medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S02 -->
3. Centrifuge the tube at 200g for 5 min at 8 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S03 -->
4. Aspirate the supernatant completely. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S04 -->
5. Proceed as described in Steps 13 and 14 of the main PROCEDURE, and overlay with the appropriate expansion medium (500 µl per well for 24-well plates or 250 µl per well for 48-well plates) supplemented with 10 µM ROCK inhibitor (Y-27632). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S05 -->
6. Fully change the medium every 3-4 days. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S06 -->
7. Remove the ROCK inhibitor after 6 days in culture. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S07 -->
8. Suspend the cell aggregates in the appropriate basement matrix (50 µl per well for 24-well plates or 25 µl per well for 48-well plates), gently pipetting up and down until the cell aggregates are completely resuspended. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S08 -->
9. Seed 50 µl or 25 µl of the basement matrix suspension as a droplet in the center of each required well on a prewarmed 24/48-well plate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S09 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Work quickly and keep the suspension cold to prevent the matrix from solidifying in the tube. Avoid generating air bubbles. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S10 -->
10. Incubate the plate for 5-10 minutes at 37 °C or until the basement matrix polymerizes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S11 -->
11. Overlay with the appropriate expansion medium in each well (500 µl per well for 24-well plates or 250 µl per well for 48-well plates). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S12 -->
12. Change the medium every 3-4 days, and passage the organoids by repeating Steps 8-15 every 5-7 days as desired. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S13 -->
13. Proceed as described in Steps 13 and 14 of the main PROCEDURE, and overlay with the appropriate expansion medium (500 µlreserved. per well (24-well plates) or 250 µl per well (48-well plates)) supplemented with 10 µM ROCK inhibitor (Y-27632). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S05 -->

## FACS Sorting of Ductal Stem Cells

### 2-3 h

1. Resuspend the ductal structures in 5 ml of prewarmed TrypLE solution supplemented with 5 µl of DNaseI (10 mg/ml). After adding the TrypLE solution, use a narrowed glass Pasteur pipette (obtained by holding a glass Pasteur pipette in a flame to narrow the aperture to ~1/4 of its original size) and pipette up and down five times. Incubate the mixture at 37 °C for 5-10 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S01 -->
2. Check the TrypLE digest solution every 2 minutes using a bright-field microscope. Stop the digestion when the majority (90-95%) of material consists of single cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Do not overdigest the material. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S03 -->
3. Add 10 ml of cold wash medium to stop the digestion, and pellet the material by centrifuging at 300-400g for 5 minutes at 8 °C. Discard the supernatant, add 10 ml of wash medium, resuspend the pellet, and pellet again by centrifuging at 500g for 5 minutes at 8 °C to wash out any remaining TrypLE. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S04 -->
4. Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 5 ml of wash medium. Filter the resuspended material into a 50-ml centrifuge tube through a 40-µm filter to leave only single cells in the tube. Count the number of cells using a standard hemocytometer or similar device. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S05 -->
5. Divide the material into a negative control and a sample for antibody staining, transferring 10% and 90% of the material, respectively, into suitable FACS tubes. Pellet the cells by centrifuging at 400g for 5 minutes at 8 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S06 -->
6. Resuspend the pellets in 2 ml of blocking solution (DMEM/GlutaMAX with 2% FBS, 2 µl of DNaseI (10 mg/ml), and 10 µM ROCK inhibitor (Y-27632)), and incubate the mixture on ice for 10-20 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S07 -->
7. Pellet the cells by centrifuging at 400g for 5 minutes at 8 °C. Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 500 µl of wash medium supplemented with 0.5 µl of DNaseI (10 mg/ml) and 10 µM ROCK inhibitor (Y-27632). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S08 -->
8. For sample tubes undergoing staining, add the desired antibody and incubate the tubes on ice in the dark for 1 hour. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S09 -->
9. Add 3 ml of wash medium and pellet the cells by centrifuging at 400g for 5 minutes at 8 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S10 -->
10. Discard the supernatant and repeat step 8. Resuspend the pellet in 500 µl of wash medium supplemented with 10 µM ROCK inhibitor (Y-27632). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S11 -->
11. Go to the FACS sorter and, after gate separation, sort the desired cells into a collecting tube containing culture medium supplemented with 10 µM ROCK inhibitor (Y-27632). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S12 -->
12. Pellet the sorted material by centrifuging at 500g in a table-top microcentrifuge for 5 minutes at 8 °C. Seed the cells as described in Step 2 of the main PROCEDURE. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S13 -->

## Human Liver Dissociation

### 2 h

1. After surgical excision, keep the tissue cold (4 °C) in basal medium until processing. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** PAUSE POINT: Tissue can be stored in basal medium at 4 °C for up to 48 hours. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S02 -->
2. Under aseptic conditions, place the tissue into a 100-mm Petri dish and mince it into pieces of roughly 0.5-1 mm³ using fine scissors. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S03 -->
3. Transfer the minced tissue to a 15-ml centrifuge tube and add ~10 ml of ice-cold wash medium. Gently pipette up and down with a 10-ml pipette to wash the liver pieces. Allow tissue pieces to settle, discard ~7.5 ml of the supernatant (including blood cells and floating fat), and repeat this wash step once. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S04 -->
4. Remove as much supernatant as possible from the pellet, add ~4-5 ml per gram of tissue of prewarmed human liver digestion solution, and incubate the mixture at 37 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S05 -->
5. After 30 minutes of incubation, pipette the digestion solution up and down vigorously with a 10-ml pipette, and check an aliquot for the presence of single cells. If few single cells are present, return the solution to 37 °C. Perform this check every 10 minutes for up to a maximum of 90 minutes. Stop the digestion when the suspension contains 80-100% single cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S06 -->
6. When digestion is complete, add cold wash medium to increase the volume to 15 ml. Pass the digested material through a 70-µm filter, and add ice-cold wash medium to increase the volume to 50 ml. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S07 -->
7. Pellet the material by centrifuging at 300g for 5 minutes at 8 °C. Discard the supernatant, add cold wash medium to a volume of 15 ml, and transfer the resuspended material to a 15-ml centrifuge tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S08 -->
8. Pellet the material by centrifuging at 300g for 5 minutes at 8 °C. Remove and discard the supernatant, wash the pellet twice with wash medium and once with 10 ml of basal medium for the final wash, pelleting the material by centrifuging at 300g for 5 minutes at 8 °C each time. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S09 -->
9. If you wish to enrich for ductal cells before the growth of organoids, sort the cells as described in Box 2 before proceeding to Step 2. If cell sorting is not required, proceed to Step 2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S10 -->

## Organoid Maintenance and Cryopreservation

### Day 0 (Pre-seeding)

1. CRITICAL: Prewarm multiwell plates for seeding at 37 °C for 1 hour to overnight. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S129 -->

### Within 7 d

1. Grow the organoids for 10-15 days after isolation or for 5-7 days between passages. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S01 -->

### Passaging

1. Disrupt the basement matrix containing the organoids (drops in the center of the well) by scraping and pipetting up and down using 500-1,000 µl of basal medium and a 1,000-µl pipette. Transfer the organoid suspension to a 15-ml centrifuge tube, add cold basal medium to the top (~13-14 ml), and pipette up and down three to five times to remove the basement matrix. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S01 -->
2. Centrifuge the tube at 100-200g for 5 minutes at 8 °C. Aspirate the supernatant, leaving ~2 ml in the tube, and resuspend the organoids in this remaining medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S02 -->
3. Hold a glass Pasteur pipette in a flame to narrow its aperture (by ~1/2). Using this narrowed Pasteur pipette, pipette the remaining 2 ml of supernatant up and down five to ten times to break the organoids. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S03 -->
4. Add cold basal medium to fill the tube, and centrifuge it at 200-250g for 5 minutes at 8 °C. Aspirate the supernatant completely. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S04 -->
5. At this step, it is possible to freeze the organoids for storage. If freezing organoids, follow the procedure described in Box 3. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S05 -->

## Organoid Maintenance and Passaging

### 10-15 d after isolation

1. Grow the organoids for 10-15 days after isolation or for 5-7 days between passages. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: The interval between passages may differ slightly depending on the initial density of organoids seeded after isolation. Prevent organoids from overgrowth (indicated by the medium turning yellow). Similarly, do not passage the organoids too soon. The general split ratio for a confluent well is 1:4-1:6. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S02 -->
2. Disrupt the basement matrix containing the organoids (drops in the center of the well) by scraping and pipetting up and down using 500-1,000 µl of basal medium and a 1,000-µl pipette. Transfer the organoid suspension to a 15-ml centrifuge tube, add cold basal medium to the top (~13-14 ml), and pipette up and down three to five times to remove the basement matrix. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S03 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Do not pool more than three wells (24-well plates) or six wells (48-well plates) together, so the basement matrix can be properly washed from the organoids. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S04 -->
3. Centrifuge the tube at 100-200g for 5 minutes at 8 °C. Aspirate the supernatant, leaving ~2 ml in the tube, and resuspend the organoids in this remaining medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S05 -->
4. Hold a glass Pasteur pipette in a flame to narrow its aperture (by ~1/2). Using this narrowed Pasteur pipette, pipette the remaining 2 ml of supernatant up and down five to ten times to break the organoids. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S06 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Do not dissociate the organoids into single cells. If a Pasteur pipette cannot be narrowed, use 200-µl filter tips and pipette up and down until organoids are completely disrupted into fragments. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S07 -->
5. Add cold basal medium to fill the tube, and centrifuge it at 200-250g for 5 minutes at 8 °C. Aspirate the supernatant completely. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S08 -->
6. At this step, it is possible to freeze the organoids for storage. If freezing organoids, follow the procedure described in Box 3. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S09 -->

## Seeding and Initial Culture

### 30 min

1. CRITICAL: Prewarm tissue culture plates at 37 °C for 1 hour to overnight. For mouse cells, adherent plates can be used. For human cells, suspension plates are required to avoid cell attachment to the plate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S01 -->
2. Remove the supernatant and resuspend the desired number of cells or duct structures (1,000 cells or 50 duct structures per well of a 24-well plate) in an appropriate basement matrix for seeding (i.e., Matrigel for mouse material and BME2 for human material). Use a volume of 50 µl per 24-well plate and 25 µl per 48-well plate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Basement matrix (BME2 and Matrigel) requires thawing on ice at 4 °C overnight. Basement matrix will solidify at room temperature (25 °C), so it is important to work quickly and to keep the basement matrix cold throughout the process. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S03 -->
3. Seed the material by adding a droplet of basement matrix to the center of each well, preventing the drop from touching the edges to avoid cell attachment to the plate. Incubate the cells for 5-10 minutes at 37 °C or until the basement matrix is solidified. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S04 -->
4. Overlay the droplet with isolation medium (500 µl per well for a 24-well plate and 250 µl per well for a 48-well plate) according to the corresponding tissue, as specified in the Reagent Setup and Supplementary Table 1. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S05 -->
5. Incubate the material under standard tissue culture conditions (37 °C, 5% CO2). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S06 -->
6. In the case of mouse and human livers, after 3-4 days replace the isolation medium with normal liver expansion medium (without Wnt and Noggin). If seeding single cells, continue to supplement the medium with 10 µM ROCK inhibitor (Y-27632) for the first 6 days in culture. Change the medium every 3-4 days. Organoids should be visible within 7 days and ready for passaging before 14 days of culture. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S07 -->

## Viral Transduction of Organoids

### ~1 week after starting selection

1. ~1 week after starting selection, passage the organoids according to Steps 7-16 and overlay with the appropriate medium supplemented with puromycin (1 µg/ml). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B10-T2-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: For continued culture, keep organoids in puromycin-containing medium to prevent silencing of transgenes. If transducing liver organoids, proceed to Box 4 if you wish to differentiate the cells to hepatocytes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B10-T2-S02 -->

### after 2-3 d

1. Selection: Start selection after 2-3 days by adding puromycin (1 µg/ml) to the expansion medium appropriate for the organoid type being cultured. For mouse organoids, if possible, use medium supplemented with Wnt3a and 10 µM ROCK inhibitor (Y-27632). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B10-T1-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: It is important not to wait longer than 2-3 days to start selection. Noninfected organoids will grow, and upon addition of puromycin they will burst, which may cause the death of infected organoids. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B10-T1-S02 -->
2. If you have transduced mouse organoids, remove Wnt3a and ROCK inhibitor from the medium when the fragments have formed cystic organoids that reach full size. Continue supplementing with puromycin (1 µg/ml) for continued selection. If you have transduced human organoids, retain Wnt3a and ROCK inhibitor throughout the selection period. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B10-T1-S03 -->

### Days 6 and 7

1. Preparation of organoid cells for transduction: Dissociate the organoids to single cells, as described in Step 17A(i-v). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B10-T0-S01 -->
2. Remove the supernatant, resuspend the cells in 1 ml of complete medium, and transfer the cells to a 1.5-ml tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B10-T0-S02 -->
3. Centrifuge the cells at room temperature at 600g for 5 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B10-T0-S03 -->
4. Remove the supernatant and add 20 µl of transduction medium containing polybrene. Resuspend the pellet by tapping the tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B10-T0-S04 -->
5. Keep the cells on ice at 4 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B10-T0-S05 -->
6. Retroviral transduction (Days 6 and 7): Combine organoid fragments with 250 µl of the retroviral solution from Step 17B(xiv) in one well of a 48-well plate. Mix gently by slowly pipetting using a 1,000-µl pipette. Seal the plate with Parafilm. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B10-T0-S06 -->
7. Centrifuge the plate at 32 °C at 600g for 1 hour. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B10-T0-S07 -->
8. Carefully remove the Parafilm and incubate the plate at 37 °C for 5-6 hours. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B10-T0-S08 -->
9. Transfer the infected organoid fragments and transduction medium from the well to a 1.5-ml tube and spin it at room temperature at 600g for 5 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B10-T0-S09 -->
10. Discard the supernatant and incubate the tube containing the pellet on ice for 5 minutes to cool it down. Add 25 µl of the appropriate basement matrix and resuspend the pellet by pipetting slowly up and down. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B10-T0-S10 -->
11. Seed the material by adding a 25-µl droplet of basement matrix:cell mixture to the center of each well (48-well plate). Incubate the plate for 5-10 minutes at 37 °C or until the basement matrix is solidified. Add 250 µl of transduction medium without polybrene to the wells, and incubate the plate in a tissue culture incubator under standard culture conditions (37 °C, 5% CO2). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B10-T0-S11 -->

## Viral Transduction Production

### Day 0

1. Transfection of Plat-E cells for virus production (Day 0): Seed ~5 × 10^6 cells into a 150-mm dish with 20 ml of medium (DMEM + 10% FBS) in the presence of puromycin (1 µg/ml) and blasticidin (10 µg/ml). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T0-S01 -->

### Days 2 and 3

1. Days 2 and 3: After 2-3 days, when the Plat-E cells have reached 30-40% confluence, change the medium to 15 ml of DMEM + 10% FBS without puromycin and blasticidin before transfection. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T1-S01 -->
2. Prepare two tubes containing 12 µg of retroviral DNA construct in 750 µl of Opti-MEM. Prepare one tube containing 60 µl of Lipofectamine 2000 in 1.5 ml of Opti-MEM. Incubate both tubes at room temperature for 5 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T1-S02 -->
3. Add 750 µl of the Lipofectamine:Opti-MEM solution mixture to the 750 µl of DNA:Opti-MEM solution. Mix by pipetting and incubate the mixture at room temperature for 25-30 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T1-S03 -->
4. Add the complete mixture to the medium of Plat-E cells, and carefully shake the plate to ensure equal distribution of the DNA:Lipofectamine complexes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T1-S04 -->
5. Incubate the Plat-E cells with the transfection mixture overnight. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T1-S05 -->

### Days 3 and 4

1. Days 3 and 4: The following day, change the medium (DMEM + 10% FBS without puromycin and blasticidin) to remove the transfection reagents. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T2-S01 -->
2. Culture the cells in this medium for 2 days. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T2-S02 -->

### Days 5 and 6

1. Virus collection (Days 5 and 6): Attach a 0.45-µm filter to a 25-ml syringe and place it on top of a 50-ml ultracentrifuge tube. Remove the piston and add all of the medium from the 150-mm dish using a 25-ml pipette. Add the piston and pass the medium through the filter. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T3-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** ! CAUTION: Make sure that the ultracentrifuge tube does not fall over. If you are unsure about its stability, use a retort stand to hold the tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T3-S02 -->
2. Spin the tube at 4 °C at 8,000g for 12-16 hours. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T3-S03 -->

### Days 6 and 7

1. Preparation of the viral solution and cell suspension (Days 6 and 7): Carefully collect the tube from the ultracentrifuge. A small white pellet should be visible. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T4-S01 -->
2. Transfer the pellet in 500 µl-1 ml of the culture medium from the high-speed centrifuge tube to a 1.5-ml microcentrifuge tube using a 1,000-µl pipette. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T4-S02 -->
3. Spin the tube at room temperature at 8,000g for 5 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T4-S03 -->
4. Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 250 µl of transduction medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B09-T4-S04 -->

## References

- [1] Culture and establishment of self-renewing human and mouse adult liver and pancreas 3D organoids and their genetic manipulation. — https://doi.org/10.1038/nprot.2016.097
